issue: Is criminal contempt under 18 U.S.C. § 401 automatically classified as a Class A felony under 18 U.S.C. § 3559(a), or is its classification determined by the most analogous underlying offense or a case-by-case approach?

sides.position: Criminal contempt should automatically be classified as a Class A felony under § 3559(a), based on the literal reading of § 401.
cases: United States v. Wright, 812 F.3d 27 (1st Cir. 2016)

sides.position: Classification under § 3559(a) turns on the statutory maximum of the most analogous underlying offense, not a literal reading of § 401.
cases: United States v. Broussard, 611 F.3d 1069 (9th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Carpenter, 91 F.3d 1282 (9th Cir. 1996) (per curiam)

sides.position: Classification is decided through a flexible, case-by-case sentencing approach rather than a uniform rule.

quote: Circuits are divided on the proper classification of criminal contempt.
cite: United States v. Stacy Owens, No. 25-5015 (6th Cir. 2025)
